Before your first inquiry

Getting started

You don’t need to arrive with a finished research plan. Start with a question that interests you, then check whether the lab offers a suitable undergraduate role.

01

Build a small, focused list.

Compare the research topic, required coursework, weekly hours and semester commitment. Save several groups you could explain a clear interest in. For a faculty or center lead, undergraduate intake still needs to be established.

02

Read the lab’s instructions.

Open “Details & sources” for the evidence behind each listing. Check the intended term, contact, prerequisites and any application form. When two sources disagree, confirm the point with the lab. Use the application route it requests.

DIS enrollment, credit, supervision and registration requirements vary by department. Ask your academic advisor before assuming a placement will earn credit.

03

Send a specific introduction.

Read a recent lab paper or project description. Explain the topic that interests you, one relevant experience, and the hours and term you can commit. Edit every bracketed placeholder in the CELLS template, attach your résumé, and proofread the recipient and attachment.

04

Confirm the arrangement.

Before accepting, ask what your work will involve, how you will be trained, who supervises you, and whether the role is paid, volunteer or for credit. Confirm weekly hours, duration, location and required training. An inquiry, public listing or application does not guarantee an offer.

If a lab does not reply, one brief follow-up after about a week is a reasonable courtesy; follow any instructions that set a different timeline or ask for no further emails.

05

Use the campus routes.

UROP is a structured program with its own application and matching process. Honors in the Major, department research courses and other CRE opportunities have separate eligibility and deadlines.

Outreach & résumé templates

The supplied CELLS email templates are editable below. Download your edited text before closing this file; message edits are not stored.

Make the message your own
  • Replace every bracketed placeholder with accurate details.
  • Use a specific paper, project or finding from the professor’s work.
  • State the term and weekly hours you can realistically commit.
  • Attach your résumé and check the lab’s requested application method.

Copy and download work on the text currently in each field. If your browser blocks clipboard access, the text downloads instead.

Copy the wording below into your email app. Editing, copying and downloading need a full browser.

First inquiry

Subject: Undergraduate Research Inquiry — [Research Topic] — [Term]

Dear Professor [Last Name],

My name is [Your Name], and I am a [year] majoring in [major] at [university]. I am reaching out to express my interest in contributing to your research group during [term].

I came across your [paper or project] on [specific topic] and was particularly interested in [specific finding, method, or research question]. [One sentence explaining why this aspect interests you or how it connects to something you have studied or explored.]

Through [relevant coursework, project, or experience], I have [specific example of what you learned or accomplished], developing a foundation in [relevant skill or subject]. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this background to your research while learning additional methods. I can commit [number] hours per week during [term].

Would you be open to a brief conversation about possible undergraduate research opportunities, either with you or a member of your group? I have attached my resume for your reference.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best regards,

[Your Full Name]
[Major] | [University]
[University Email]
Follow-up

Subject: Re: Undergraduate Research Inquiry — [Research Topic] — [Term]

Dear Professor [Last Name],

I wanted to briefly follow up on my previous email regarding undergraduate research opportunities in your group for [term].

I remain very interested in your work on [research topic] and would appreciate the opportunity to discuss whether there might be a way to get involved.

Thank you again for your time and consideration.

Best regards,
[Your Full Name]

Scope, evidence & upkeep

Sources & review

This is a CELLS member resource built from public FSU directories, lab pages, application instructions and project records. It is a reviewed snapshot dated October 13, 2026, and does not update itself.

Created for CELLS members

This directory was created by Macin Bennetts, Scholarship & Internship Chair of FSU CELLS, to help members explore research opportunities and prepare thoughtful outreach.

426Research records, including historical entries
163Projects in the current public UROP database
520Page retrieval checks in this audit

What this directory establishes

The 426 records comprise 122 labs or research groups, 23 programs and routes, 87 faculty or center leads, and 194 UROP records. Of the UROP records, 163 were publicly listed in the current database and 31 are historical records retained from the original guide. Closed and expired records are hidden in the directory until you include them.

This is not a census of every unpublished lab or every available seat. An institutional research profile establishes an interest lead; it does not establish undergraduate eligibility or capacity. Dated invitations, undated application routes and inquiry contacts are labeled separately. Requested UROP staffing totals are not counts of remaining seats.

The latest pass checked 357 linked sources and 163 UROP detail pages: 509 of the 520 checks returned HTTP 200. Eleven retrievals failed or were blocked. A successful retrieval alone does not establish that a page is complete or current. Limited retrievals are marked in record details, and failures are not treated as evidence that a lab has closed.

How conflicts were handled

Lab-specific instructions and dated notices take priority over older or undated departmental language. Where public sources disagree, the detail view shows the conflict and asks members to confirm it. Application forms are kept distinct from study-participant recruitment. Faculty affiliations are cross-checked where possible; unconfirmed undergraduate intake is labeled.

What changed in this audit
Problem foundChange made
An undated application route could look like a live opening.Use conservative availability labels, separate dated semester invitations and show unconfirmed capacity.
The Social Development Lab action pointed to a contact also used for study participants.Use the lab director address confirmed in the linked practicum PDF.
Source selection could open a faculty profile instead of the stated application instructions.Give specific verified application pages priority and use neutral source labels when no application is established.
Hidden directory leads and omitted department names could cause incomplete name/discipline results.Global search, explicit record-type sections, accent-insensitive matching and department indexing.
Lab and UROP status options were mixed; section changes reset work.Contextual facets and independent preserved directory/shortlist states.
Downloaded-file browser storage is unreliable across file copies.Validate stored IDs and provide portable shortlist backup and merge import.
Oversized introductory material, small text, narrow three-column rows and successive CSS overrides reduced clarity.A compact CELLS header, a coherent stylesheet, readable typography and responsive flat directory rows.
Some controls were small or discovered only after scrolling; modal focus and navigation needed clearer behavior.Visible section controls, labeled fields, 44px primary targets, keyboard focus handling and source/status text independent of color.
CSV could preserve an invited status after a deadline expired; the detail year was hardcoded.Export displayed/current status separately from source status, derive date years and protect CSV cells.
Restoring paginated rows immediately after print() could happen before a nonblocking print capture.Prepare full filtered output for beforeprint and restore it after printing.

Check the note behind a record

Each record has its own evidence note and direct source links. Search here to inspect a particular correction or qualification.

RecordEvidence note

Usability refinement

This revision preserves the complete reviewed research dataset. It shortens the mobile opening area and records, keeps search scoped to your chosen section, retains filter and page context when you clear a query, and adds full side-by-side comparison for two or three saved records. Application/source actions appear before the full eligibility section and stay visible in a mobile detail action bar.

Saved-list JSON files from the previous version remain compatible. Printed comparisons include complete requirements and source citations.

Keep the guide useful

Before applying, open the source and confirm dates, instructions and capacity. If you find an error, send the lab name, changed fact and official source link to a CELLS executive board member. The board should review dated windows before each semester and check departmental rosters when updating the file.

The seal was supplied by CELLS. The design uses FSU’s published garnet and gold palette, Open Sans, and EB Garamond as an open serif companion. This student resource is not an official university vacancy database.

Validation limit: the local-file browser preview was blocked by the execution environment. Static markup, data and interaction tests were performed; visual browser verification and assistive-technology testing remain incomplete.
